evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.11: perniciem meam cum magnā calamitāte reī pūblicae esse conjūnctam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The farmers’ word for a ruined crop, hail or blight (Donatus on Ter. Eun. 79, where a courtesan is nostrī fundī calamitās, the ruin of our farm).

terms.gloss: misfortune; in comedy mostly the punishment or thrashing in store for someone
terms.register: vōx plērumque cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; Liv. semel
terms.comment: Mostly ante-classical and post-Augustan, not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: clādēs calamitāsque, intemperiēs modo in nostram advēnit domum
phrases.english: ruin, disaster, a very tempest has just come into our house

phrases.latin: Sed ecca ipsa ēgreditur, nostrī fundī calamitās.
phrases.english: But look, here she comes herself, the ruin of our farm.

phrases.latin: modo sīs venī hūc: inveniēs īnfortūnium
phrases.english: just you come here: you’ll find trouble

sources: Lewis & Short: calamitas · Lewis & Short: infortunium
